scoreProvenance: OpenScore Lieder releases its scores under CC0 (https://github.com/OpenScore/Lieder#license-and-acknowledgement). The MusicXML identification reads 'Transcribed by markpearse from IMSLP #522898' and carries rights 'OpenScore (CC0)'. Exact downloaded MXL bytes match the SHA-256 pinned in this config; no printed-edition imprint beyond that IMSLP reference is asserted.

Source part P1 is the Voice (one treble line with lyrics); P2 is Piano (two staves with explicitly numbered MusicXML voices 1/2 and 5/6). Each source voice is a separate MIDI track in one simultaneous compilation, not inferred from register. Two print-object="no" rests in piano bars 11 and 13 are omitted by the converter. Voice labels are encoding identities, not separated audio stems.

Nonstandard MusicXML other-dynamics texts ('a tempo', 'dolce marcato', 'poco rall.') are preserved as printed words via otherDynamicsWords, because LilyPond 2.24.4's converter would otherwise emit invalid identifiers; no note or rhythm changes.

Initial grace: the piano's opening D-flat2 acciaccatura (voice 5) gives every MIDI track one common 43/384-quarter lead, retained once in bar 1's quarter extent. The guarded grace-priming adapter places nonprinting grace skips before the opening triplet groups of the other voices so that the engraving does not duplicate the initial clef/key/time glyphs; the converted event arrays are identical with and without that priming (995 notes).

Recording: Johanna Gadski, soprano, with Frank La Forge, piano, Victor 87026, 14 January 1908 (content/listen module). The side couples La Forge's 'How Much I Love You' first; only the Beach song that follows is aligned, and the earlier song is outside the aligned span.

Key and tuning (MEAS): the voice traces D-flat5 'year's' (65.3 s), B-flat4 'spring', E-flat5 'day's', C5 'morn', G-flat5 'hill-', E-flat5 'pearled', the A-flat5 'right' hold (95.9–100.3 s), G-flat5/E-flat5/F5 'All's right with the' (101.6/102.6/104.2 s) and D-flat5 'world' from about 106.8 s, matching the D-flat source without transposition; global tuning estimate −17 cents.

Inspection (MEAS, not aural): a per-note dominant-pitch ranking over MIDI 64–89 places the written vocal pitch first in 30 and within the top three in 52 of 58 sung notes; the six misses are short notes under louder piano chords. This voice-dominated acoustic side has faint piano; individual accompaniment attacks are not individually established.

Initial-grace contexts synchronized by silent grace skips, retaining source notes and main-time durations: Original lc6212179.mxl P2 measure 1 direct note index 27 is the visible D-flat2 eighth acciaccatura in voice 5/staff 2, before the bass D-flat3 on the first beat. Synchronize the other voices with nonprinting, nonsounding grace skips after their original initial attributes (before the opening triplet group where a voice begins with one); retain every pitched grace and all main-time note/bar durations. This follows LilyPond's documented grace-skip remedy for key/time synchronization: https://lilypond.org/doc/v2.24/Documentation/notation/special-rhythmic-concerns#grace-notes .

endpointMeasurements.label: first
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS, cached transfer (pitch-band tables; work/beach-years-at-the-spring-58-76.png). La Forge's song ends at about 59.2 s; isolated short events at 61.1–63.1 s precede near-silence, and Beach's bar-1 chord bands (D-flat3/A-flat3/F4/A-flat4) rise from about −48 to −21 dB at 64.48–64.66 s (librosa onsets 64.39/64.56/64.61 s), followed by the voice's D-flat5 'year's' at about 65.26 s. The module's 52 s section marker and an earlier 56–57 s estimate fall inside the end of the preceding song and the pause. The first score attack is the piano's D-flat2 grace, whose own band is not measurable in this acoustic recording; the first window places it immediately before the chord rise, about 0.05 s (43/384 quarter) ahead — a documented placement, not a measurement of the grace. The final bar-29 chord is the only late event with a jump of the D-flat6/F6/D-flat7 band (−46 to −23 dB at 111.2 s); its F5 band rises at the same time. Numerical and visual inspection only; no aural review is claimed.

endpointMeasurements.label: bar-26-world-D-flat5
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS: performed q77.112 is the bar-26 downbeat: the voice's D-flat5 on 'world' with the piano's D-flat bass and F5/A-flat5/D-flat6/F6 triplet chord. After the loud F5/G-flat5/F6 'with the' chords at 104.2–106.4 s, total energy dips at 106.6 s; the D-flat5 band then rises from −43 to −24 dB (106.4→106.8 s) and the D-flat6 band from −52 to −30 dB at 106.8 s. The unconstrained candidate placed this downbeat at 106.34 s, before that rise. Disclosed source-pitch fitting constraint, not independent or aural validation.
